questions.q: How many times do you need to create a linked service for a single data store you'll reference repeatedly?
options: Once — it's reused across as many datasets and pipelines as needed
Once per dataset that uses it
Once per pipeline that uses it
Every time you run a pipeline
questions.explain: A linked service is a reusable connection. Create it once per data store, then reference it from any number of datasets and pipelines.

questions.q: Where in Data Factory Studio do you create a new linked service?
options: The Manage hub, under Linked services
The Monitor hub
The Home page only
You can't create one from the Studio UI at all
questions.explain: Manage (the briefcase icon) → Linked services → + New opens the connector gallery for creating a new linked service.

questions.q: Which property of a linked service's JSON definition is required and specifies which connector it is?
options: type
connectVia
annotations
description
questions.explain: type identifies the connector — for example AzureBlobStorage or AzureSqlDatabase — and is required. connectVia is optional and defaults to the Azure Integration Runtime.

questions.q: What's the core distinction between a linked service and a dataset?
options: A linked service defines how to connect; a dataset defines which specific data inside that connection
They're two names for the exact same thing
A dataset defines the connection; a linked service defines the specific file or table
A linked service can only be used by one dataset at a time
questions.explain: The linked service is the connection itself. The dataset points to a specific table, file, or folder reachable through that connection — one linked service can back many datasets.

questions.q: What does the connectVia property of a linked service control?
options: Which integration runtime actually executes the connection
The name of the dataset that will use this linked service
Whether the linked service is enabled or disabled
The pipeline that owns this linked service
questions.explain: connectVia references an integration runtime — Azure, self-hosted, or SSIS — and defaults to the Azure Integration Runtime if left unspecified.
